subject: Archaeology
title: Hammurabi's Code: The First Written Laws
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Hammurabi's Code: The First Written Laws.

hook.text: King Hammurabi of Babylon carved 282 laws onto a stone pillar in 1754 BCE — including 'an eye for an eye.'

buildup.text: The laws cover everything: theft, marriage, wages, medical fees, and building standards.

discovery.text: French archaeologists found the stele at Susa, Iran, in 1901. An Elamite king had stolen it from Babylon centuries earlier.

twist.text: The punishments varied by social class. Injuring a nobleman cost more than injuring a commoner. Justice was not equal.

climax.text: Hammurabi's Code was not the first law code — earlier ones exist — but it is the most complete and influential.

punchline.text: The first detailed law code had 282 rules.

quiz.question: What made Hammurabi's Code controversial by modern standards?
options: It banned all forms of religious practice
Punishments varied by the social class of the victim
It applied only to citizens of Babylon, not foreigners
